cur:monumental-santa-cecilia-apse.summary: Against a deep blue sky with red-edged clouds, Christ stands at the centre on a cloud, raising his right hand in blessing and holding a scroll, while the hand of God crowns him from above. He is flanked by Saints Paul, Cecilia and Pope Paschal I (with the square halo of the living, holding a model of the church) on one side and Peter, Valerian and Agatha on the other; below, the twelve lambs process from Bethlehem and Jerusalem. The composition deliberately recalls the 6th-century apse of Santi Cosma e Damiano.
facts: Pope Paschal I rebuilt the church in 822 and moved the relics of Saint Cecilia here from the Catacombs of Saint Callixtus.
Paschal I appears in the mosaic with a square halo, the conventional sign that the person was still alive when the image was made.

cur:objects-ringelheim-crucifix.summary: This monumental wooden figure of the crucified Christ hangs with arms stretched straight out, his body upright, head slightly bowed, wearing a long loincloth. The calm, dignified figure shows a Christ who reigns from the cross even in death. Together with the Gero Cross in Cologne it is one of the earliest large-scale crucifixes of the Middle Ages.
facts: German Wikipedia records that Bishop Bernward of Hildesheim gave the monumental crucifix to the convent of Ringelheim, where his sister Judith was abbess around 1000, possibly on the occasion of her death.
cur:objects-ringelheim-crucifix.notes: Material details beyond 'wood' are not verified. The photo shows the crucifix as displayed in the Hildesheim Dommuseum (2019).
